governing_table.code: Los Angeles Plumbing Code (LAMC Chapter IX, Article 4) = 2025 California Plumbing Code (Title 24, Part 5), Chapter 4, adopted by reference
governing_table.edition: 2025 California Plumbing Code, in force in Los Angeles from 2026-01-01 (Ordinance 188797)
governing_table.table: CPC Table 422.1, Minimum Plumbing Facilities (Section 422.1). The building code's Chapter 29 table is not used in California.
governing_table.quote: Chapter 29 of the 2025 California Building Code (CBC) refers to the 2025 California Plumbing Code (CPC) (Title 24, Part 5) to determine the minimum number of the plumbing fixtures required for each type of building occupancies. In accordance with the CPC, as amended by the Los Angeles Municipal Code (LAMC), the minimum number of plumbing fixtures are shown in CPC Table 422.1, except that CPC Table 4-2 shall be used for those uses regulated by the Office of Statewide Hospital Planning and Development (OSHPD)

other_quotes.quote: 422.1 Fixture Count. Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of building occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 422.1.
(Not Adopted By The State Of California) Refer To California Plumbing Code, Title 24, Part 5

other_quotes.quote: The Los Angeles Plumbing Code adopts by indicated reference portions of the 2025 California Plumbing Code (CPC) of Title 24 of the California Code of Regulations (CCR).

governing_table.note: LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-095 'Plumbing Fixtures' (effective 01-01-2026, revised 03-20-2026) is the city's own statement of which table applies.

amendments.text: Los Angeles adopts CPC Chapter 4 by reference and does not amend Section 422 or Table 422.1. Its Chapter 4 changes are about other things: urinal standards and flush volume (CPC 412.1 and 412.1.2 replaced by LAMC 94.412.1 and 94.412.1.2), self-closing or metering faucets in public restrooms (94.407.2.4.1) and dishwasher water use (94.414.5, 94.414.6). The 2026 ordinance (188797) touches only 94.407.2.4, 94.407.2.4.1, 94.414.5 and 94.414.6 in Division 4. The adoption sentence for Chapter 4 was last set by Ordinance 187719 (2022 cycle) and was not restated in 2026; 'CPC' is now defined as the 2025 edition (LAMC 94.205.0). California's own state amendments are already inside the 2025 CPC table (the [BSC], [DSA-SS] passages quoted under rules). LADBS adds plan-check guidance, not amendments, in P/BC 2026-095: existing-building options, a restaurant under 50 occupants treated as Group B, no customer fixtures for take-out counters of 2,500 sq ft or less, and a table for community facilities not listed in Table 422.1.
amendments.quote: Chapter 4 of the CPC is adopted by reference except CPC Sections 412.1 and 412.1.2 are not adopted, and LAMC Subsections 94.407.2.4, 94.412.1, 94.412.1.2, 94.414.4, and 94.414.5 are amended or added to read as follows:

other_quotes.quote: 94.407.2.4.1. All faucets in public restrooms shall be self-closing or self-closing metering faucets. Metered faucets shall deliver a maximum of 0.20 gallons (0.76 L) per metering cycle.

sex_split.text: 50 percent male, 50 percent female of the total occupant load, unless submitted information shows a different split. The table's tiers are then read per sex.
sex_split.quote: 422.1.1 Fixture Calculations. The minimum number of fixtures shall be calculated at 50 percent male and 50 percent female based on the total occupant load. Where information submitted indicates a difference in the distribution of the sexes such information shall be used to determine the number of fixtures for each sex.

local_quote.quote: The minimum number of plumbing fixtures are assumed to be based on 50 percent male and 50 percent female users.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number; with several occupancies in one building, add the fractions first, then round up. Tiers cover 'any fraction thereof'.
rounding.quote: Where applying the fixture ratios in Table 422.1 results in fractional numbers, such numbers shall be rounded to the next whole number. For multiple occupancies, fractional numbers shall be first summed and then rounded to the next whole number.

other_quote.quote: 1 The figures shown are based upon one fixture being the minimum required for the number of persons indicated or any fraction thereof.

urinal_substitution.text: Three rules. (1) Extra urinals beyond the minimum may each replace one water closet, down to two-thirds of the required water closets. (2) California lets a water closet be installed in place of each required urinal, so a men's room can be all stalls. (3) Women's water closets must be at least the men's water closets plus urinals; this often raises the women's count above the table tier.
urinal_substitution.quote: 4 For each urinal added in excess of the minimum required, one water closet shall be permitted to be deducted. The number of water closets shall not be reduced to less than two-thirds of the minimum requirement.

other_quotes.quote: [BSC & DSA-SS] The substitution of a water closet for each urinal shall be permitted provided the total number of fixtures installed complies with Table 422.1.

3 The total number of required water closets for females shall be not less than the total number of required water closets and urinals for males. [BSC] This requirement shall not apply when single occupancy toilet facilities are provided for each sex in an A or E occupancy with an occupant load of less than 50. Either a. The required urinal shall be permitted to be omitted or b. If installed, the urinal shall not require a second water closet to be provided for the female.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate facilities for each sex are the rule. One single-user toilet room for both sexes is allowed at a total occupant load of 10 or less (any occupancy) or 50 or less in business and mercantile occupancies. Separate rooms are also not required where an all-gender room has every water closet in a privacy compartment. LADBS extends the 50-or-less business exception to restaurants with fewer than 50 occupants.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: 422.2 Separate Facilities. Separate toilet facilities shall be provided for each sex. Exceptions [Not adopted for OSHPD 1, 2, 3, 4 & 5]: (1) Residential installations. (2) In occupancies with a total occupant load of 10 or less, including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (3) In business and mercantile occupancies with a total occupant load of 50 or less including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (4) Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms have fixtures designed for use by both sexes and the water closets are installed in privacy compartments.

occupant_load.text: Occupant load comes from the California Building Code (Table 1004.5) or from the plumbing code's own Table 4-1 'Occupant Load Factor', by function of space. The 2025 edition calls this table 4-1; no 'Table A' appears in Chapter 4 of the 2025 text. Table 4-1 factors (square feet per occupant): business/office 150; dining/drinking/lounge 30; commercial kitchen 50; classroom through 12th grade 30; classroom beyond 12th grade 50; mercantile 100. Hallways, stairs, toilet rooms, mechanical rooms and closets may be left out. Table 4-1 gives far fewer occupants for a restaurant than the egress table would, so which one the plan checker accepts changes the count.
occupant_load.quote: The total occupant load and occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the California Building Code. Occupancy classification not shown in Table 422.1 shall be considered separately by the Authority Having Jurisdiction. [...] Exception: [BSC & DSA-SS] Using occupancy classification, described as function of space, determine occupant load factor from Table 4-1 Occupant Load Factor, of this chapter.

other_quotes.quote: [BSC & DSA-SS] The total occupant load shall be determined in accordance with the California Building Code or Table 4-1 Occupant Load Factor.

TABLE 4-1 OCCUPANT LOAD FACTOR: [BSC & DSA-SS] ... Conference, dining/drinking, lounge (portable seating/table space) 30 ... Business (office, sales/soliciting, administration, food processing, courtroom, ambulatory clinic) 150 ... Education (classroom) Through 12th grade 30 ... Kitchen/food prep (commercial) 50
Accessory areas such as, but not limited to, hallways/corridors, stairways, ramps, toilet rooms, mechanical rooms, closets and fixed equipment, may be excluded.
The occupant load shall be determined using the CPC Table 4-1, titled, 'Occupant Load Factor' in accordance with CPC Section 422.0 and CPC Table 422.1.

Provide plumbing fixture analysis based on occupant load calculated in accordance with occupant load factors matching the function of each space per CPC Table 4-1 or CBC T1004.5.(CPC Table 422.1, P/BC 2026-095)

when_the_table_applies.text: New buildings, additions, and changes of occupancy that raise the occupant load. Replacing partitions in an existing restroom does not trigger a recount.
when_the_table_applies.quote: Table 422.1 applies to new buildings, additions to a building, and changes of occupancy or type in an existing building resulting in increased occupant load.

worked_examples.how: 50 occupants at 50/50 = 25 male, 25 female (422.1.1). B row: male water closets tier for 25 = 1; urinals tier for 25 = 1; female water closets tier for 25 = 2. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 1+1 = 2, so female = 2. Lavatories: male 1, female 1. Alternative: at a total occupant load of 50 or less a business occupancy may instead have one single-user toilet room for both sexes (422.2 Exception 3). A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

100 occupants at 50/50 = 50 male, 50 female (422.1.1). B row: male water closets tier for 50 = 1; urinals tier for 50 = 1; female water closets tier for 50 = 3. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 1+1 = 2, so female = 3. Lavatories: male 1, female 1. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

200 occupants at 50/50 = 100 male, 100 female (422.1.1). B row: male water closets tier for 100 = 2; urinals tier for 100 = 1; female water closets tier for 100 = 4. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 2+1 = 3, so female = 4. Lavatories: male 2, female 2. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

400 occupants at 50/50 = 200 male, 200 female (422.1.1). B row: male water closets tier for 200 = 3; urinals tier for 200 = 2; female water closets tier for 200 = 8. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 3+2 = 5, so female = 8. Lavatories: male 3, female 4. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

50 occupants at 50/50 = 25 male, 25 female (422.1.1). A-2 row: male water closets tier for 25 = 1; urinals tier for 25 = 1; female water closets tier for 25 = 1. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 1+1 = 2, so female = 2 (raised from 1). Lavatories: male 1, female 1. The note 3 waiver ([BSC], single-occupancy rooms for each sex) is for an occupant load of less than 50, so it does not reach 50. Below 50 occupants LADBS treats the restaurant as Group B and allows one single-user room (P/BC 2026-095, VII). A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

100 occupants at 50/50 = 50 male, 50 female (422.1.1). A-2 row: male water closets tier for 50 = 1; urinals tier for 50 = 1; female water closets tier for 50 = 2. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 1+1 = 2, so female = 2. Lavatories: male 1, female 1. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

200 occupants at 50/50 = 100 male, 100 female (422.1.1). A-2 row: male water closets tier for 100 = 2; urinals tier for 100 = 1; female water closets tier for 100 = 3. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 2+1 = 3, so female = 3. Lavatories: male 1, female 1. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

400 occupants at 50/50 = 200 male, 200 female (422.1.1). A-2 row: male water closets tier for 200 = 3; urinals tier for 200 = 1; female water closets tier for 200 = 4. Note 3: female water closets not less than male water closets + urinals = 3+1 = 4, so female = 4. Lavatories: male 2, female 2. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

50 occupants at 50/50 = 25 male, 25 female (422.1.1). E row: male water closets 25/50 = 0.50, rounded up = 1; urinals 25/100 = 0.25, rounded up = 1; female water closets 25/30 = 0.83, rounded up = 1. Note 3: female not less than 1+1 = 2, so female = 2 (raised from 1). Lavatories 25/40 = 0.62, rounded up = 1 for each sex. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

100 occupants at 50/50 = 50 male, 50 female (422.1.1). E row: male water closets 50/50 = 1.00, rounded up = 1; urinals 50/100 = 0.50, rounded up = 1; female water closets 50/30 = 1.67, rounded up = 2. Note 3: female not less than 1+1 = 2, so female = 2. Lavatories 50/40 = 1.25, rounded up = 2 for each sex. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

200 occupants at 50/50 = 100 male, 100 female (422.1.1). E row: male water closets 100/50 = 2.00, rounded up = 2; urinals 100/100 = 1.00, rounded up = 1; female water closets 100/30 = 3.33, rounded up = 4. Note 3: female not less than 2+1 = 3, so female = 4. Lavatories 100/40 = 2.50, rounded up = 3 for each sex. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

400 occupants at 50/50 = 200 male, 200 female (422.1.1). E row: male water closets 200/50 = 4.00, rounded up = 4; urinals 200/100 = 2.00, rounded up = 2; female water closets 200/30 = 6.67, rounded up = 7. Note 3: female not less than 4+2 = 6, so female = 7. Lavatories 200/40 = 5.00, rounded up = 5 for each sex. A water closet may be installed in place of each urinal (422.1.1 [BSC & DSA-SS]).

Table note 3 (women's water closets at least men's water closets plus urinals) is applied in the worked examples. It lifts the women's count above the table figure in two of the twelve cases: restaurant at 50 occupants and school at 50 occupants (1 becomes 2). Confirm with LADBS plan check that it is applied this way.
Occupant load: LADBS accepts CPC Table 4-1 or CBC Table 1004.5. The CBC table was not read here. For a page, state counts by number of occupants, or use Table 4-1 factors only.

Viewer text comes out column by column; the male/female and fixture-column assignment follows the header order (water closets, urinals, lavatories) and matches the dining and office rows repeated in LADBS's own bulletin table. Glance at printed pages 70-71 in the viewer before publishing.
